[G4] Is the outlier definition and removal rule stated (and applied before or after splitting)? -> not_reported. No outlier definition or removal rule; code/forest.R uses every row of each outcome subset.
The loop starting at line 15 reads datS, the per-iteration variable of the loop at line 4; this loop's own per-iteration variable is datR. It uses the value left over from the earlier loop.

Methods: 'Standardised mean differences (SMDs) with 95% CIs were calculated as the difference in means between groups divided by the pooled SD'. The before-after analyses call rma(measure="SMD", m1i=Post.Mean, sd1i=Post.SD, n1i=Post..N., m2i=Pre.Mean, ...), i.e. metafor's SMD for two independent groups, not a standardised mean change for paired data; the correlation between pre and post scores is not reported anywhere.

Methods describe the between-group analysis as 'exercise training versus usual care'. code/forest.R computes yi = datT$yi - datC$yi and vi = datT$vi + datC$vi, i.e. the difference of two within-group (pre-post) SMDs, not a between-group SMD of post-training means. The paper does not state that the between-group effect is a difference of within-group changes.

Methods: 'A minimum of four comparisons were used to ensure meaningfully pooled data'. The code applies no such filter: every outcome subset in readdata.R is passed to rma() regardless of the number of rows (e.g. Figure.a15 SF36.GH has 4 rows, Figure.a20 TypeIIa.percent has 4). The rule is stated but not implemented in the released code.
